## Course Description The bottleneck on what you can build is no longer *what you already know* — it's your workflow discipline and your ability to direct an agent. This course teaches students to use tools like [Claude Code](https://www.claude.com/product/claude-code) to build ambitious things they don't yet know how to build, while developing the professional engineering workflows — version control with Git and GitHub, continuous integration with GitHub Actions, and deployment with GitHub Pages — that make agentic work sustainable and trustworthy. Each week pairs a hands-on workflow concept (taught live in class) with an ambitious take-home build in an unfamiliar domain: a deployed personal website, a novel in an author's voice, a video game, a data pipeline, a simulation experiment, and more. The arc of the course follows a "trust gradient," moving from high-touch, back-and-forth collaboration with an agent toward orchestrating specialized agents that work for long stretches under human supervision. By the end, students will have strong, transferable engineering workflow skills, the ability to work with code and data through an agent, and — most importantly — the ability to teach themselves new domains so they can tackle harder systems in the future. ## Prerequisites Students must have completed at least one programming course (e.g., CSCI 1012 or equivalent) or have comparable experience working in at least one programming language. You do not need to be an expert, but you should be comfortable reading code, following the logic of a program, and recognizing when something is wrong — these are the skills that let you supervise an agent rather than blindly trust it. **Students with zero coding experience will find this course very difficult.** # Learning Objectives Having successfully completed this course, students will be able to: - Direct an AI agent to build real products in domains they haven't learned before. - Use Git, GitHub, and pull requests fluently as everyday version control and collaboration tools. - Set up continuous integration with GitHub Actions and deploy to the web with GitHub Pages. - Debug agent-built systems and use agents to diagnose and resolve issues, with automated review. - Orchestrate specialized agents (planning, coding, testing) into a supervised pipeline. - Teach themselves a new domain using an agent — the meta-skill that outlasts any single tool. # How the Course Works The course runs on a **dual spine**. Every week pairs: - **A workflow concept, taught hands-on in class.** Our 2.5-hour weekly session is a workshop. We learn a workflow skill by *doing it together* in real time — the first time you make a repository, open a pull request, or set up continuous integration, you'll do it live in class. - **An ambitious take-home build.** Each week's individual assignment is a build in an unfamiliar domain that forces you to apply that week's workflow skill on your own, at higher stakes. The sequence follows a **trust gradient**: we begin with high-touch, back-and-forth collaboration with an agent and progress toward orchestrating specialized agents that work for long stretches under your supervision. See the [schedule](schedule.qmd) for the week-by-week plan. # Assignments ## Participation & Attendance **Attendance will be taken and is the primary driver of your participation grade.** In-class work is hands-on and ungraded — but it is *practice for the build you do at home*. The take-home builds assume the skills we develop together in class, so missing class costs you twice: once on participation, and again on a much harder homework. Plan to attend in person every week. ## Individual Builds Each week (Weeks 1–8) you complete one **build**: an ambitious project in a domain you likely haven't worked in before. Each build is delivered as a **GitHub repository that includes the full conversation history** with the agent. Grading focuses on prompt quality, evidence of iterative collaboration, final product quality, and thoughtful use of the week's workflow skill. There are 8 builds, each worth 5% of your grade. ## Team Project Throughout the semester you'll work in **teams of 3–4** on an open-ended project of your own design — the one piece of fully open-ended work in the course. It is broken into milestone deliverables (proposal, interim report, final report, presentation). See the [project overview](project/0-overview.qmd) for details. # Grading Final grades will be calculated as follows:
Item | Weight | Notes -----|--------|---------------------------------- Individual Builds (8) | 40% | 8 builds, each worth 5% Team Project: Proposal | 5% | Teams of 3–4 (Week 6) Team Project: Interim Report | 10% | (Week 11) Team Project: Final Report | 25% | (Week 15) Final Presentation | 10% | (Week 16) Participation / Attendance | 10% | Yes, attendance is taken
## Generative-AI Use Policy Using AI agents is not "cheating" in this course — **it is the core skill being taught**. For individual builds you are *required* to use an agentic coding tool and to disclose your full conversation history as part of your submission. You remain fully responsible for the correctness, quality, and originality of everything you submit: read what the agent produces, run it, and fix it when it's wrong. Detailed disclosure requirements appear in each assignment. # Course Policies > *Detailed policies — late work, re-grades, academic integrity, attendance > thresholds, and university-required statements (DSS, religious holidays, CAPS, > nondiscrimination, recording) — will be merged in here from the working > syllabus draft (`class-factory.md`).*
